$comment: The suggestion lifecycle, once. Every consumer reads THIS file: packages/data generates a typed module from it, docs/LIFECYCLE.md is generated from it, and tui/src/tui.rs embeds it at compile time. Nothing is published yet, so there is no legacy vocabulary to carry — a status is written exactly as its id. Do not restate any of this in prose anywhere — a sixth copy is how the previous five got out of sync. Regenerate with `kaizen docs`; `kaizen docs --check` fails when a generated artifact has drifted.

phases.title: Capture
phases.actor: the skill that hit the problem
phases.summary: A skill finishes a run, notices something that cost it, and files it. Write down everything the next reader will need, because they were not there. Capture is cheap and never blocks the run that files it.

phases.title: Triage
phases.summary: Decide whether the problem is real, still present, and correctly described — then label it. Re-read the scope file at HEAD before anything else: months pass between capture and triage, and a suggestion whose fix already landed is superseded, not work. Labelling changes no code, so it needs no approval.

phases.title: Plan
phases.summary: Turn a validated problem into something that can be approved: the change itself as a real patch, and the validation plan that will prove it worked. A plan without a validation plan is a guess with a diff attached.

phases.title: Decide
phases.summary: The only attended phase. You are shown the change and the validation plan together and say yes or no. Nothing reaches this phase without both, which is the point: approving an idea nobody has written is how a queue fills with decisions that cannot be drained.

phases.title: Apply
phases.summary: Land the patch as one commit per suggestion, into a clean tree, on a writable target. The commit carries a Kaizen-Suggestion trailer, so `git log --grep=Kaizen-Suggestion` is the ledger for free and `git revert <sha>` is the undo.

phases.title: Verify
phases.summary: Run the validation plan written during planning against the change that actually landed. This is the phase that makes the loop closed rather than open: without it, applied means nothing more than the diff did not conflict.

statuses.label: Recorded
statuses.help: Filed with its context and waiting for triage. Nobody has judged it yet.

statuses.label: Triaged
statuses.help: Confirmed to still be a real problem at HEAD, and labelled. Ready for someone to plan a fix.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.help: A patch and a validation plan both exist. This is the only status that can be approved.

statuses.label: Approved
statuses.help: You said yes to a specific patch. It lands on the next drain.

statuses.label: Applied
statuses.help: Landed as a commit. The server sets this after git succeeded — it cannot be set by hand.

statuses.label: Verified
statuses.help: The validation plan passed against the landed change. Done, and provably so.

statuses.label: Failed
statuses.help: It landed and the validation plan did not pass. Goes back for a new plan rather than starting over — the problem is still real and still triaged.

statuses.label: Rejected
statuses.help: You said no. The file stays on disk as a record and stops being offered.

statuses.label: Superseded
statuses.help: The problem is gone — already fixed by other work, or the file it named no longer exists. Records where the fix actually lives so the finding is not re-filed.

fields.heading: Context
fields.help: What happened, in enough detail that someone who was not there can judge it months later. The run, the inputs, the command, the actual error text.

fields.heading: Suggestion
fields.help: What to change. A concrete edit where one is obvious, not a wish.

fields.heading: Why it matters
fields.help: What it costs to leave alone, and how often. This is what scoring reads.

fields.heading: Evidence
fields.help: The receipts: command output, file:line, a PR or run URL. Triage re-checks the claim against HEAD and cannot do that from a summary.
low, medium or high. Leave blank rather than guessing — a wrong label outranks a missing one in the queue, which is worse.
determinism, structural, behavioral, content, tooling or hygiene.
bug, guardrail, feature, performance, clarity or debt.
The file the fix lands in — one scope is one fix, and suggestions sharing it share a fate. Name the path a script would live at even when it does not exist yet.
0-3 on the determinism ladder. A rung of 2 or 3 must say in one sentence why the rung below does not work.
When the problem was last confirmed to still exist at HEAD, and against which commit. Without this there is no way to tell a live finding from one the codebase already moved past.

fields.heading: Plan
fields.help: The change, concretely: which files, which edits, and what deliberately stays out.

fields.heading: Validation
fields.help: How we will know it worked — the command to run and the result that counts as passing. A self-check for a rung-1 script, a test for a code change, a named observable behaviour otherwise. This is what the verify phase executes.
The real diff, stored beside the suggestion, passing `git apply --check`. A described patch is not a patch.
The commit. Set by the server, never by hand.
When the validation plan was run against the landed change, and what it returned.

rungs.title: Harness enforces it
rungs.detail: A hook, a permission rule, a CLAUDE.md line. Cannot drift, cannot be skipped.

rungs.title: A script decides
rungs.detail: Shell returning a verdict. Testable, greppable, identical every run.

rungs.title: A written rule
rungs.detail: Prose re-read and re-interpreted every run. Fine when the input genuinely varies.

rungs.title: Left to reasoning
rungs.detail: Nothing written down. Where most recorded failures came from.
